source: Petar Puhmajer, «Stancija de Franceschi u Segetu kod Umaga», Mala biblioteka Godišnjaka zaštite spomenika kulture Hrvatske sv. 20, Ministarstvo kulture RH, Zagreb 2019, ISBN 978-953-312-048-5 — with Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria: note storiche» (Parenzo 1879).
timeline: Venice grants the Seget and Đube lands to families fleeing Greece and Montenegro.
Captain Vincenzo Cuchich of Šibenik sells the land to the Venier, a noble house of Venice. The contract mentions only a pasture — nothing is built yet.
The de Franceschi flee Crete after the Candian War and reach Istria.
Nicolò and Marc'Antonio de Franceschi, sons of Giorgio, buy all of Catarina Bernardo Venier's possessions in Venetian Istria, Seget among them.
The year cut into a portal on the estate.
Umag grants them citizenship, and all their heirs with them.
The year and the initials M A · F cut into the stone well-head — Marc'Antonio Franceschi.
Alvise dies; his sons divide the estate, and the deed lists the palace room by room.
Seget is drawn on the Franciscan cadastre, the palace already standing with its chapel.
Carlo De Franceschi, writing at Gologorica's other branch, records them as «la nobile famiglia De Franceschi, attuale posseditrice, emigrata dall'isola di Candia».
One De Franceschi family is still counted at Seghetto in the Istrian census.
people: father of the two brothers who bought Seget
civil and military physician; married Crissulla Marulli in 1727; eleven children
his wife — a Greek name, Chrysoula Marouli, carrying the Cretan origin
son; lawyer at Koper, died without heirs
son; his family settled at Brtonigla
son; lived at Seget; the family genealogy records him as «Dragomanno alla Porta ottomana» — dragoman at the Ottoman court. Married Francesca Borella, six children
archives: fond de Franceschi — letters, contracts, wills, inventories and accounts over several centuries. Box 1 holds the «Albero genealogico della Famiglia de Franceschi», about 1896, naming every member with dates of birth, death and marriage.

fond de Franceschi — box 3 holds the «Albero genealogico dei Signori de Franceschi, Umago», 1927, listing the male members only. Box 3 also holds a notebook of copied letters, «Raccolta di varie lettere eleganti e familiari», about 1830.
foglio 16, sezione 20, 548 B 20 — the 1818 cadastral sheet showing the estate.
carlo: Carlo's own book records «Golgoriza (Moncalvo)» among the first Slavic place-names to appear in Istrian diplomas — the earliest documented mention of Gologorica, written by a man born there.
A ducale of 24 March licenses Leonardo Fioravanti, «Sabba de Franceschi» and Vincenzo dall'Acqua, all of Bologna, to bring a hundred and twenty-four families to Pola to clear land.
Among the noble families then living at Pola he lists the Franceschi, «venuti da Capodistria» — come from Koper.
His source for the Fontane and Umag colonists is «il sig. Giambattista De Franceschi deputato al Consiglio dell'Impero», who drew it from his own family archive.

voce.heading: What the 2020 article adds
voce.lead: A full feature on the estate — «La tenuta de Franceschi di Seghetto» — ran in «la Voce del popolo» on 23 May 2020, written out of the conservation survey the City of Umag commissioned in 2016 when Seget entered the Croatian Ministry of Culture's programme for cultural property. A copy has been in the family's own files ever since. This archive did not open it until September 2026.

origins.w: The article opens the family «nobili di origine romana» with a Ferramondo de Franceschi who fought Odoacer, king of the Heruli. Legend, and printed as such — but note that a Ferramondo de Franceschi is still being christened at Umag in the twentieth century.
The family is said to have moved to Padua, then Venice, then to have emigrated to Crete with others in this window.
They defended the ports of Calus, Lemiores and Sabionera with nine hundred vassals of their county, at their own expense.

Marcantonio Querini, duke of Candia, confirmed the counts de Franceschi in the privilege of mero et mixto imperio — delegated jurisdiction — on 30 December, for services «nelle più ardue ricorrenze, col somministrar gente, haveri et cavalli». Zaccaria Mocenigo renewed the comital title on 16 December 1688.

When Candia fell, Morosini's galleys took off the Venetian families who asked to go home. On the way the fleet met a terrible storm; the ships were wrecked and only a small number of refugees were saved. The de Franceschi were among the survivors, and at Venice were admitted to the «veneta cittadinanza originaria».

On 16 July, «causa gli urgenti bisogni della Serenissima», the brothers Carlo, Giovanni Battista, Costantino and Domenico made a donation of 100,000 ducats. The Senate raised the family from the Order of Secretaries to the Sovrano Ordine Patrizio and inscribed it in the Libro d'Oro of Venetian nobility.

Aggregated to the nobility of Parenzo in 1774 and to the Noble Council of Capodistria in 1802; confirmed noble by the Emperor Francis I of Austria; entered on the Official List of the Italian Nobility as «nobili di Capodistria», recognised in 1931.

The brothers Nicolò and Marc'Antonio de Franceschi, sons of Giorgio, bought Seghetto together with everything the noblewoman Caterina Bernardo, widow of Pietro Valier, held in Istria — and from 1730 the citizenship of Umag for themselves and their descendants.

house.heading: The house, and the arms over its door
house.text: Marc'Antonio de Franceschi (1671–1758), a civil and military physician, began the manor after the purchase. The great works came in 1843–45, commissioned by Giorgio de Franceschi (1788–1865): a grand staircase in the eastern part, painted decoration, and the façade given two giant pilasters and a tympanum — which is where the arms are. Thirty years later the eastern wing went up, holding a library of over four thousand volumes bought from the booksellers of Trieste, Pirano, Buje and Poreč, together with an archive. Some scholars held it one of the richest libraries in Istria. It was devastated during the twentieth century and the room itself was later partitioned into smaller ones.
house.blazon: Troncato di azzurro e d'oro al leone rampante al naturale.
house.blazonEn: Per fess azure and or, a lion rampant proper. This archive has drawn the Seget arms until now with the lion named and not drawn, because no blazon for it had been found. Here is one — and it is the arms on the tympanum of the house itself, not a coat sold by surname. Over the monumental gate there is a second, older achievement: an eighteenth-century cartouche with an oval shield.
house.rest: Behind the palace stood the coach-house, the granaries, the colonists' dwellings and a nineteenth-century oil mill whose presses and a dozen stone oil jars — the «pile» — survived until recently. A crenellated tower to the north-west watched the property; a «specola» stood a few hundred metres off. The de Franceschi traded wine, oil, cereals, timber and birds, live and slaughtered, and their colonists formed a wind band under a maestro Pietro Moro that did rather well.

chapel.heading: The chapel of Santa Costanza
chapel.text: Built in the eighteenth century as patrician families did, with the saint's relics venerated on the high altar and two doors — one to the outside and one into the house. Inside, a small neoclassical altar of black and grey marble, and an altarpiece of the Assumption with Saints Anthony and Catherine. A seventeenth-century St Lucy on canvas has been restored by Kristina Bin Latal and Silvo Šarić of the Restoration Institute at Jursići. A St George painted on wood guards the inner door. A reliquary holds relics of St Andrew the Apostle, St Benedict Abbot, St Giles Abbot, St Anthony Abbot, St Romuald, St Felix martyr, and — «ex osse exusto» — St Lawrence. A Madonna and Child, probably Renaissance, is visible in photographs of the mid-twentieth century and is now gone. After years of neglect the chapel has been restored and reopened to worship.

public.heading: What they did with the position
rows: Member of the General Council of the Department of Istria
A physician; volunteered with Garibaldi in the wars of the Risorgimento

Between them, mayors of Umag for a century. Giovanni Battista was a scholar and a collector of unpublished manuscripts of the town's history — and, in Carlo's book, the deputy to the Imperial Council who supplied the Seget documents from his own family archive.
President of the Umag Philharmonic and of the Mutual Aid Society; councillor of the Congregation of Charity, the Rural Bank and the Cooperative Purchasing Society
An engineer. Built a brick works at Spinel that the Great War ruined, and designed and directed the church and campanile of Materada
public.branches: The family split in two: the Seghetto branch held Seghetto, Giubba and Spinel; the Umag branch held Rosazzo, Macalè — formerly Casoni — and Carsette.
public.guests: The house received the Venetian admiral Angelo Emo (1731–1792), who led the fleet to its last victories against the Barbary corsairs in 1769 and 1784, and Pietro Kandler, the father of Istrian historiography.

voce.caveat: A newspaper feature, not a monograph — but written off the 2016 conservation survey and consistent at every checkable point with Carlo's own 1879 account and with Puhmajer's study. Its deep origins — Rome, a prefect against Odoacer, the move to Padua — are the family's own tradition as the nobiliary literature repeats it, and are printed here as that and nothing more.

diet.heading: Giovanni Battista in the Istrian Diet, January 1895
diet.lead: The Austrian National Library's newspaper archive was searched in September 2026 for the surname beside the name of this archive's own parish. Eight issues came back. The fullest is «Il giovine Pensiero» of Pola for 16 January 1895, which prints the stenographic record of the opening of the Provincial Diet of Istria at Parenzo — and a De Franceschi is running it.
diet.quote: Il signor capitano provinciale apre la seduta e concede la facoltà di parlare all'on. Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, che a nome della maggioranza intera così si esprime…
diet.en: The provincial captain opens the session and gives the floor to the honourable Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, who speaks in the name of the entire majority. What he then says is that the events of the past year had so moved public opinion as to give the Italians of Istria occasion to raise before the Imperial Government their strongest complaints and most energetic protests at the unjust and partisan way they are treated in everything touching their national life.
roles: Elected one of the session's revisori — its tellers.
A signatory of the interpellation asking how the Government justifies opening the Diet without having appointed a vice-president.

A signatory of Dr Bubba's motion against the bilingual signs being put up in the Istrian district courts — the great language quarrel of the 1890s, and the motion says the Italians of Istria were offended in their rights by a Slavicisation «not requested by the Slavs living in the province» themselves.
Acting as scrutatore in the election of a substitute assessor, where all twenty ballots carried one name.
Speaking again for the majority, asking the Captain to use his good offices to persuade the assessors who had resigned to stay in post.

gallignana.heading: And on the same order paper, Gallignana
gallignana.text: Among the bills before the session: «progetto di legge sull'istituzione dei nuovi Comuni locali di Pisino, Novacco, Lindaro, Terviso, Gallignana, Pedena» — a bill for the establishment of new local communes, this archive's own parish among them. In January 1895 the Diet of Istria was legislating Gračišće into a commune, and the man leading the majority in that chamber carried the surname.

who.heading: And this is very probably the Seget man
who.text: Carlo's book of 1879 credits its Seget documents to «il sig. Giambattista de Franceschi deputato al Consiglio dell'Impero» — a deputy to the Imperial Council in Vienna, drawing on his own family archive. The 2020 feature on the estate lists among the mayors of Umag between 1815 and 1918 a Giovanni Battista, «studioso e collezionista di manoscritti inediti della storia umaghese» — a scholar and collector of unpublished manuscripts of the town's history. And here, in 1895, a Giovanni Battista de Franceschi leads the Italian majority of the Istrian Diet. Three sources, sixteen years apart, and on the face of it one man: the Umag branch in politics.
who.caution: Stated as the likely reading, not a proven identity. The Diet report gives no patronymic and no place, and Giovanni Battista is the commonest name in every branch of this surname.

diet.source: «Il giovine Pensiero», Pola, 16 January 1895, pages 1–2. ANNO ID igp18950116; images from the ONB's IIIF service. The issue carries nine occurrences of the two search terms and they are all in this report.

confirmed.heading: And in 1898 an obituary settles it
confirmed.text: «Il Popolo Istriano» of 17 September 1898 reports a society's annual meeting and its roll of members dead in the year. «Speciale menzione fa di Giov. Batt. de Franceschi, capo dei deputati italiani alla Dieta, uscito dalla patriotica famiglia di Seghetto, esempio di gentilezza e ospitalità; dice che sedette, soldato fedele alla consegna, lunghi anni nel Parlamento di Vienna, nella Dieta e nei Consigli delle principali nostre istituzioni, né tradì mai in nessun posto, neppur con l'ombra di un pensiero, quello che era il suo, quello che è il nostro ideale.»
confirmed.en: Special mention of Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, head of the Italian deputies in the Diet, **out of the patriotic family of Seghetto**, an example of courtesy and hospitality; he sat, a soldier faithful to his orders, long years in the Parliament of Vienna, in the Diet and in the councils of our principal institutions, and never in any post betrayed, not even by the shadow of a thought, what was his ideal and is ours.
confirmed.why: That closes the identification this archive had left open. The man leading the Italian majority of the Istrian Diet in 1895 is the Seget man — «uscito dalla patriotica famiglia di Seghetto» — and the «Parlamento di Vienna» is exactly the Consiglio dell'Impero to which Carlo's book of 1879 says «il sig. Giambattista de Franceschi deputato al Consiglio dell'Impero» belonged, when he handed Carlo the Seget documents out of his own family archive. Same man, three sources, nineteen years apart. He died in 1898.
confirmed.also: And in «Il giovine Pensiero» of 19 January 1895 he signs the majority's resolution not as a member but as its chair: «G. B. de Franceschi mp. presidente, Dr. Becich mp. segretario».

umago.heading: They ran Umago for a hundred years
umago.lead: Found in Rino Cigui's «Contributo all'araldica di Umago», in the «Atti» of Rovigno, volume 24 of 1994. Under Venice the town had a Venetian rector sent out yearly — Balbi, Corner, Priuli, Bembo, Barozzi, a Salamon in 1764. Then Venice fell, and the town began electing its own. Cigui lists them.

mayors.n: Dott. Giacomo de Franceschi di Seghetto
mayors.note: «of Seghetto» — the manor this page is about

mayors.n: Giov. Batt. de Franceschi di Seghetto

umago.count: Eight mayors between 1815 and 1918, and four of them De Franceschi. Cigui adds that under Austria a mayor was re-elected repeatedly and stayed in office for many years, so eight men cover the century between them. Two are given in the list by the name of the estate: «di Seghetto».
umago.after: And it did not stop in 1918. Of the three commissari who governed Umago under Italy, two were De Franceschi — Ettore again, and a Ferramondo de Franceschi. A Luigi de Franceschi appears later among the nine prefectural commissioners. The family was in the town hall, on and off, from the fall of Venice to the Second World War.

historian.heading: And one of them wrote the town's history
historian.text: From Cigui's edition of Pietro Kandler's «Cenni storici di Umago» in the same journal, volume 34 of 2004: Kandler was among the first, «assieme al canonico Francesco Roselli ed a Giovanni Battista de Franceschi», to attempt a systematic reconstruction of Umago's past. The note on him reads: «Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, cultore di studi storici e autore della raccolta ‘Manoscritti inediti relativi alla Storia di Umago'. Fu podestà di Umago nella seconda metà dell'Ottocento.»
historian.why: A collector of historical studies, author of a gathering of unpublished manuscripts on the history of Umago, and mayor of the town in the second half of the nineteenth century. This archive had already identified the Giovanni Battista de Franceschi who led the Italian majority in the Istrian Diet in January 1895 as the Seghetto man, on the strength of his 1898 obituary. Here he is again, from the other side: not only a politician but a working local historian with a manuscript collection to his name. Whether that collection survives, and where, is not known here.

woods.heading: And the woods they owned are still on the map
woods.text: The Venetian cadastre of Verteneglio of 1775, edited in the «Atti» volume 22 of 1992, lists among the woods of the commune: «Bosco detto Capitania di Nicolò Franceschi e di Giure Turina», «Bosco detto Slavai del Signor Nicolò de Franceschi», and «Bosco alla Stanza detta Valentich di Nicolò Franceschi». At Matterada in 1775–76 a Nicolò Franceschi is one of five co-owners of a wood by Ive Ferletta's house.
woods.then: The name stuck to the ground. A boundary description of 1819 walks the surveyor along «il fosso dividente sempre il Bosco de Franceschi dal bosco de consorti Coronica» to a tall stone marked F.F., and a study of Istrian wood-names in volume 23 of 1993 lists «Bosco de Franceschi a Verteneglio» among the standing toponyms of the province. A wood named for the family, on the register, half a century after Nicolò bought it.

umago.source_umago: Rino Cigui, «Contributo all'araldica di Umago», Atti vol. XXIV (1994); «Umago. Cenni storici di Pietro Kandler», Atti vol. XXXIV (2004), pp. 421–472; «La toponomastica del comune catastale di Verteneglio», Atti vol. XXII (1992), pp. 255–286; and the wood-name study in vol. XXIII (1993). All read from the Internet Archive copies, September 2026.

dossier.heading: The house, the library, the band and the oxen
dossier.lead: «La Ricerca», the bulletin of the Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, ran a study of the noble estates of the Umago country in December 2004, built from the archives of Trieste, Pazin and Rijeka. Half of it is about this family. It is free on the Internet Archive, and nothing in it was in this archive.

rows.lab: 1674 — the pension, and the road out of Crete
rows.text: «Nel 1674 la Repubblica di Venezia assegnò a Zorzi de Franceschi una pensione per i meriti avuti durante la guerra di Candia.» Zorzi de Franceschi was given a Venetian pension for his services in the War of Candia. After the Turkish conquest he went from Candia to Zante, and from Zante to Sebenico. A document of 1730 directs that the pension be drawn at Capodistria — «probabilmente perchè la famiglia viveva già a Seghetto». The French suspended the payment; the Austrians restored it. That is a hundred and fifty years of a Venetian war pension following one family from Crete to Istria.

«La tenuta di Seghetto era circondata da un alto muro in pietra.» An olive press, deep cellars, stables, granaries and a carriage house. A receipt of 1856 records that Luigi de Franceschi bought a carriage from Giacomo Feranda of Pisino for 260 florins.

«Nel palazzo, che con la sua grandezza domina tutta la tenuta, trovava posto una imponente biblioteca, che si dice di oltre 3.000 volumi.» A library of more than three thousand volumes, bought from booksellers at Trieste, Pirano, Buie and Parenzo. The article notes what sits with it: professors at Padua, agronomists, deputies to the parliament at Vienna, mayors of Umago, engineers.

rows.lab: And a brass band of their own tenants
rows.text: «A Seghetto operava una banda d'ottoni, formata dai coloni. Questi venivano anche pagati per venire alle prove.» A brass band at Seghetto made up of the estate's own colonus tenants, who were paid to turn up to rehearsal. It is the same band that «Il Piccolo» of 2 August 1897 has playing the anthem of Trieste on the quay at Umago — «la banda di Seghetto, propri dei signori de Franceschi» — as the excursion steamer from Trieste came alongside under a triumphal arch reading «Viva i fratelli di Trieste. Uno per tutti, tutti per uno!»

rows.lab: A brickworks that signed its bricks
rows.text: They had many properties around Umago, among them Spinel, «dove avevano persino una fabbrica di mattoni. Su questi veniva impressa la scritta Franceschi - Umago». Also a house in Venice, the Cà Franceschi, which they let, and an estate at Spinea near Treviso.

rows.lab: Kandler came to stay, and they sent him hampers
rows.text: Pietro Kandler, the father of Istrian historiography, was a visitor. The article lists what went from Seghetto to Trieste in 1849: oil, wine, wild birds in a basket, wild asparagus, fresh fruit, dead birds, fresh fish, herbs, vegetables and game. Kandler sent back veal, groceries, clothes, linen, a shotgun, books, vegetables, pasta, a jar of preserve, oysters, oranges, sweets and a hat.

rows.lab: And the names of the animals
rows.text: From a deed of division of 1870, the cattle that Countess Marianna de Franceschi née Alessandri kept at Spinel. The oxen: Gagliardo, Gardelin, Ciarin, Brum, Cavron, Morea, Rumin, Napoli, Gelen and Boscarin. The cows: Russinca, Giagoda, Brunava, Rumina, Salvinca, Moscatella, Gardellina, Ciadina, Biancolina, Gajarda, Armellina and Sernella. Twenty-two animals, named, in a lawyer's paper about splitting an inheritance.
A nineteenth-century diploma of the Istituto Satollatorio Tonico Parentino — a gastronomes' club at Parenzo — praises the mutton cutlets cooked to the recipe of Giambatta dei Franceschi.

rows.lab: The tomb, with the arms on it
rows.text: «Subito vicino c'è la tomba dei conti de Franceschi di Seghetto. Anche questa munita di stemma famigliare.» In the cemetery at Umago, next to the tomb of the counts Marcovich, is the tomb of the counts de Franceschi of Seghetto, and it carries the family arms. Another carved shield to photograph, and a second test of the blazon Carlo described privately to Kobler.

later.heading: Still farming in the 1930s
later.text: «L'Istria Agricola», the province's farming paper, in 1934: Marco de Franceschi fu Nicolò, of Umago (Seghetto), is among the breeders awarded for good bull-calves and among the keepers of public stud stations. In the classified column of the same issue: «Presso i Fr.li de Franceschi, a Seghetto di Umago, sono in vendita due falciatrici meccaniche Osborne» — two Osborne mowers for sale at Seghetto. The brothers had a rubber stamp reading Fratelli de Franceschi, and «operavano come Fratelli de Franceschi al fine di non spezzettare» the estate — trading as the brothers so as not to break the property up.
later.also: And in 1927 the same paper buries a young agronomist, Guido Vardabasso, who had begun his career «facendo della buona pratica nelle tenute degli avi materni, i De Franceschi di Seghetto di Umago» — doing his practical training on the estates of his maternal forebears, the De Franceschi of Seghetto. Among the mourners: «l'ing. Italo de Franceschi, membro della Commissione Reale». That same Italo designed the road from the centre of Umago out to the hotels at Punta, probably as part of the tourism scheme shown at the Istrian provincial exhibition at Capodistria in 1910. Thirty years earlier it was the Franco and Vardabasso families of Buie who gave forty crowns to the Lega Nazionale to honour Giovanni Battista's memory; the two houses were joined by marriage.

death.heading: «La morte di un patriota» — 25 November 1897
death.text: This archive confirmed Giovanni Battista de Franceschi as the Seghetto man from his obituary of 1898. «Il Piccolo» of Trieste had done it four months earlier and more plainly, in the notice of his death.
death.quote: L'Istria nostra è nuovamente in lutto: la morte le ha rapito un altro dei suoi cittadini più devoti: il conte Giambattista de' Franceschi di Seghetto, podestà di Umago. […] Al principio del 1895, quando tutta l'Istria attendeva dalla Dieta di Parenzo una energica voce di protesta contro le [insegne] bilingui alle sedi dei Giudizi, G. B. de' Franceschi si trovò a capo di quella maggioranza della Dieta, che con tanta nobiltà di linguaggio non disgiunta da virile energia, riaffermava l'italianità dell'Istria.
death.en: Our Istria is in mourning again: death has taken from her another of her most devoted citizens, Count Giambattista de' Franceschi of Seghetto, podestà of Umago. […] At the beginning of 1895, when all Istria was waiting for a vigorous voice of protest from the Diet at Parenzo against the bilingual signs at the seats of the courts, G. B. de' Franceschi found himself at the head of that majority of the Diet which, with so much nobility of language and no less manly energy, reaffirmed the Italianness of Istria.
death.why: Three things at once. The title — «il conte», which the newspapers give him and this archive had not. The offices, listed: podestà of Umago, deputy to the provincial Diet and to the parliament at Vienna, director of the Lega Nazionale. And the identification, made explicit: the man leading the Diet majority in January 1895, whose speech this archive published from the stenographic record, is the Seghetto man. And in the same issue, the small thing: forty crowns to the Lega Nazionale «per onorare la memoria del compianto Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, dalle famiglie Franco e Vardabasso di Buie».

dossier.candia_note: One correction to the timeline above, from the 1903 volume of the Atti e memorie della Società istriana. It says the family «trasferivasi in Istria nel 1669 ed acquistava dai Valier di Venezia la tenuta che essi nel 1623 avevano acquistata da Vincenzo Cuchich» — bought from the Valier, where this archive's timeline says Venier, and dates the purchase to the arrival rather than to 1720. The AMSI note is compressed and secondary; the timeline above follows Puhmajer, who worked from the deeds. The point of quoting it is that a third source, independently, puts this family's arrival in Istria in 1669 and out of Candia.
dossier.source_dossier: «La Ricerca», bollettino del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, nn. 42–43, December 2004 — the survey of the noble houses of the Umago country. «Il Piccolo» of Trieste, 2 August 1897 and 25 November 1897. «L'Istria Agricola», 15 February 1927 and 28 February 1934. Atti e memorie della Società istriana di archeologia e storia patria, 1903. All read from the Internet Archive copies, September 2026.
